selected.rationale: The Wellness Optimizer tracks fitness and supplements with low price sensitivity, making her a prime target for evidence-backed protein bars that solve the taste problem of traditional health snacks.
The Fitness Enthusiast works out frequently and buys supplements and functional foods, directly aligning with our protein bar product and active lifestyle demographics.
The Convenience-First Millennial values speed and impulse purchases, fitting perfectly with our snack product category and the instant delivery publisher Swiftcart.

The Gen Z Aesthete discovers through TikTok and Instagram and values playful, aesthetic-forward brand voices, matching our mission to sell protein bars that do not taste like cardboard through an engaging DTC approach.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent prioritizes meal kits and subscriptions, whereas our advertiser sells a one-off protein bar product without an established subscription model.
The Pet Parent focuses entirely on animal food and supplies, which has no logical overlap with human protein bars or our recommended grocery publishers.
The Affluent Classic prefers heritage and luxury home goods with a 50-68 age skew, whereas our protein bars target a younger 18-45 demographic with a mid price tier.
The Sustainability Buyer focuses heavily on supply chain transparency and refillable products, which does not directly align with our core pitch centered primarily around great taste.
The Value-Conscious Shopper seeks heavy discounts and bundle offers, which clashes with our mid-tier pricing and the impulse-driven nature of our snack product.
The Gifter is focused exclusively on gifting holidays and premium presentation, which contradicts our everyday grocery and snack product positioning.
